thread: Follow a calculation from gears and punched cards into electronic computers, then give it a body that can sense and move. The swarm encounters mechanical arithmetic, memory and interfaces, and robots built to explore their surroundings.

candidates.name: Heinz Nixdorf MuseumsForum
candidates.why: Its exhibition travels from numbers and mechanical information processing to early computers and personal machines: gears, keys, punched cards and circuits could all become creatures.

candidates.name: Centre for Computing History
candidates.why: A richly catalogued collection of computers, peripherals, games and software offers the swarm keyboards, screens, storage devices and curious interfaces to inhabit.

candidates.name: Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute
candidates.why: Robot and research project archives introduce machines with cameras, limbs, wheels and sensors, taking the swarm from computation into movement and perception.

candidates.name: Computer History Museum
candidates.why: Online exhibits, timelines and collections trace calculating devices, mainframes, software and early robots, with punch cards, tape drives and computer mice ready to animate.

candidates.name: The National Museum of Computing
candidates.why: Galleries and digital trails explore working historic computers and their restoration, inviting creatures made from valves, switches, paper tape and memory.

candidates.name: Science Museum Group Collection
candidates.why: Its computing and data processing objects include slide rules, logic units, early computers and calculators, alongside many other instrument collections.

candidates.name: Miraikan – The National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation
candidates.why: Exhibitions on robots and emerging technologies offer humanoid machines, communication devices and experiments in how people and machines interact.

candidates.name: Museum of Computing Machinery, University of Pisa
candidates.why: Its collection describes arithmometers, pocket calculators, the Pisan Electronic Calculator and giant Olivetti and Cray machines, with many distinctive mechanical and electronic forms.
